We investigate the computational capabilities of Constraint Handling Rules (CHRs) with multiple head rules. Our analysis reveals that this feature has significant implications: when the head rules are restricted to a single head, the CHRs become computationally limited, depending on the underlying theory; however, allowing multiple heads ensures that the system remains computationally powerful, even when the head rules are restricted to a single head, under specific conditions.

Galactic spin orientation data is used to examine the large-scale arrangement of galaxy rotation axes.  The data reveals a uniform alignment among galaxies, with their spin directions pointing towards the direction of the local cosmic flow.  The data also shows that the distribution of galaxy spin directions is consistent with a uniform pattern, and that the probability of this being due to random chance is less than one in two trillion.  The data further indicates that the orientation of galaxies is not influenced by local gravitational forces, and that the distribution of galaxy spin directions is consistent with a uniform pattern, and that the probability of this being due to random chance is less than one in ten billion.

Meta-learning techniques have gained significant attention for their ability to learn generalizable features and perform well with limited data instances. However, current approaches often overlook the complexities of real-world few-shot learning problems, where data is often noisy, and the target concept may be partially unknown. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel meta-learning framework that can handle noisy data, unknown target concepts, and limited labeled examples. Our approach is based on a probabilistic model that learns to sample from the unknown concept distribution, and we demonstrate its effectiveness in various few-shot learning scenarios, including classification, segmentation, and target discovery. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, and the accompanying code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/UCD-AIM/fsl-unknown-concept.

A novel generative deep learning approach is proposed to extract meaningful brain
features from large MRI datasets. This technique is applied to identify
distinctive cognitive and clinical profiles in a comprehensive database of
brain scans from over 37,000 individuals. By utilizing a variational
autoencoder, this method generates a condensed representation of brain structure
anatomy, which is then analyzed using advanced clustering and dimensionality
reduction techniques. The resulting brain features are used to develop a
predictive model that accurately forecasts cognitive abilities and identifies
risk factors associated with specific neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's
disease, Parkinson's disease, and schizophrenia. The brain features derived from
this approach are also shown to be highly interpretable, enabling researchers to
better understand the underlying causes of neurological disorders and identify
key biomarkers for clinical assessment.

This paper provides an update on the AI Ethics bylaws project, a collaborative effort to establish a standardized framework for discussing and publishing AI Ethics. The document outlines the three main categories of works being considered and the proposed classification system, utilizing a combination of ontological and epistemological attributes. The document also outlines the current progress and future plans for the project, including the development of a collaborative framework and ontology for AI Ethics.

We investigate the expressive power of $\omega$-word languages that can be defined using monadic second-order logic, with a focus on the impact of introducing a language containing a "neutral" letter. Our results demonstrate that the class of definable languages remains unchanged when a neutral letter is added to languages like $(\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists\forall\exists

In high-density wireless networks, rapid channel changes pose significant challenges for real-time applications. The traditional approach of periodic channel estimation, which relies on pilot signals, becomes impractical due to the vast number of required pilot symbols. To address this issue, a new method is proposed that dynamically selects pilot signals based on specific network conditions. By prioritizing pilot placement in areas with the greatest communication demands, this approach minimizes the overall cost of channel estimation. Theoretical models are developed to analyze the complexity of channel estimation, and numerical simulations are conducted to validate the proposed method's effectiveness.

The nuclear beta decay process, specifically the decay of molybdenum-99 into technetium-99 with the emission of a neutrino, is used to determine the value of the matrix element V_{ud}. This is achieved by measuring the half-life of molybdenum-99 and comparing it with the calculated decay width from standard quantum mechanics. This precise measurement, carried out by the TRIPLE collaboration, yields a value of V_{ud} = 0.9971(11) with the uncertainty primarily stemming from the measured half-life. This result is consistent with the value obtained from other methods, such as the beta decay of cobalt-54 to nickel-54.

We introduce a novel neural network architecture for image denoising that leverages identity mappings to efficiently eliminate noise from images. Our approach combines the strengths of identity mappings and a residual scale decomposition, enabling the network to focus on denoising tasks at various scales. The network's design, incorporating multiple identity mappings and residual connections, facilitates the easy implementation of additional layers, thereby enhancing its performance. Our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art denoising techniques, both visually and quantitatively, as demonstrated through experiments on multiple datasets.

In this research, we introduce a novel approach to represent multiview data by
utilizing shared components. Our proposed method, referred to as the Shared
Component Selection (SCS) framework, is grounded in the principle of maximizing
the mutual information between different views. To achieve this, we developed a
new optimization technique that incorporates a novel loss function, enabling the
identification of common features across multiple views. Our approach is
accompanied by a theoretical analysis, which substantiates its effectiveness in
extracting shared information from multiview data. Our experiments, which
involve both real-world and synthetic datasets, demonstrate the efficacy of our
SCS framework in outperforming existing methods.

We have conducted a comprehensive study of galaxies that exhibit unusual infrared properties, despite being optically normal. Our analysis of 1,500 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey's data release 7 reveals that these red outliers (RO) share a common trait - they all possess infrared colors indicative of active galactic nuclei (AGN). However, our research indicates that these red outliers are distinct from their optically-identified counterparts in several key ways. Specifically, the red outliers are more massive, with a higher mass of 10.5 compared to their optically-identified counterparts, and they exhibit a higher star formation rate. Furthermore, the red outliers are more likely to be in the early stages of their evolution, with a higher redshift of 0.5 compared to their optically-identified counterparts. Our findings suggest that these red outliers are likely the result of a merger between a star-forming galaxy and a red, massive galaxy hosting an AGN.

The development of AI systems capable of collaborating with humans effectively hinges on their ability to share moral values and make ethical decisions. However, this challenge is particularly complex due to the inherent subjectivity and cultural nuances of moral judgments. Our research focuses on moral decision-making within the context of social dilemmas, specifically in situations where individual self-interest conflicts with collective well-being. We introduce a new approach to moral decision-making in AI, grounded in the concept of reciprocal fairness, and demonstrate its potential to resolve social dilems in a fair and equitable manner.

A valuation ring over a field of positive characteristic $p$ is called a Henselian
valuation ring if it contains its residue field and meets specific Henselian
conditions. In such a ring, we demonstrate that for any $p$-th power $x^p$ of an
element $x$, there exists an element $y$ such that the equation $F(x,y)=y^p-
x^p$ holds true, where $F$ is a specific polynomial of degree $3$ in variables $y$
and $x$.

The two-dimensional Dirac equation is utilized to investigate quantum scarring within a fully chaotic environment.  By employing a two-dimensional model of a kicked system, we derive a spectral scarring indicator based on the localization of quantum states.  We then analyze the localization properties of wave functions through the lens of classical scattering theory, which provides a connection to the one-dimensional kicked system.  This allows us to establish a relationship between scarring in 2D and classical scattering properties, which we verify through numerical simulations.

The integration of autonomous vehicles and connected vehicles is poised to revolutionize the transportation industry, offering significant benefits to both drivers and passengers. Cooperative systems like CACC and platooning are expected to enhance safety and efficiency, particularly in high-density traffic conditions. This paper examines the key technologies required to implement CACC and platooning, including communication protocols, and discusses their practical applications. Additionally, it highlights the challenges associated with the adoption of cooperative systems and suggests potential solutions to accelerate their deployment.

As social media becomes increasingly influential in shaping public opinion, 
the credibility of its users has become a pressing concern. The proliferation 
of misinformation on these platforms has led to a growing need for reliable 
measures to assess user credibility. In this study, we introduce a novel approach 
to quantify social media users' credibility based on their content and interactions 
with others. By leveraging this method, we can effectively identify and isolate 
incredibly credible users who may be disseminating misinformation.

The Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) service is a key component in the development of smart transportation systems, enabling vehicles to exchange safety and infotainment information through the use of 5G networks. However, the high volume of V2X data generated by vehicles in urban areas poses significant challenges for resource allocation in 5G networks. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel network slicing framework that dynamically allocates resources to V2X services in real-time. The proposed framework consists of two stages: the offline stage, where V2X services are sliced and resources are allocated, and the online stage, where the allocated resources are adjusted based on traffic conditions. In the offline stage, the V2X services are sliced and resources are allocated using a hypernetwork-based approach, while in the online stage, the allocated resources are adjusted using a reinforcement learning-based framework. The proposed framework is evaluated using a realistic V2X traffic simulator and the results show that it significantly outperforms existing solutions in terms of resource allocation efficiency.

The effectiveness of human-robot collaboration hinges on the ability to safely interact with robots that may pose a threat due to unpredictable movements. To address this, we suggest utilizing haptic feedback to alert humans of impending potential collisions. By analyzing the human perception of haptic stimuli, we can identify the most effective haptic warnings to employ. Our research involves a study in which participants responded to tactile notifications at varying distances and intensities, and we used their responses to develop a set of guidelines for designing these warnings. The outcome of this study is a system that provides humans with timely and relevant sensory information to make informed decisions, thereby enhancing the safety of human-robot collaboration.

The world is bracing for a massive shift in urban demographics, with the United Nations forecasting a staggering 70% surge in urban population by 2050. As cities prepare to accommodate this unprecedented growth, they must address the pressing issue of sustainable development, balancing human needs and environmental concerns. The future of urban development hinges on harnessing the potential of data-driven solutions to create livable, productive, and resilient cities. This paper delves into the current state of urban development, highlighting the challenges and opportunities presented by the urbanization phenomenon.

We investigate a multi-agent caching scenario in which agents can rely on external predictions to make informed decisions, and we demonstrate that these predictions can lead to significant improvements in performance. Specifically, we show that a prediction-augmented caching algorithm achieves a competitive ratio of $O(\sqrt{\sum_{i\in I} \epsilon_i})$ when the overall prediction error is bounded, and we prove this result to be optimal within a certain constant range. Additionally, we show that this algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio of $O(\log n)$ when the individual prediction errors are bounded, and we prove this result to be optimal as well.

Accurate segmentation of medical images is crucial for medical diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the scarcity of labeled data in medical imaging hinders the application of deep learning models. To address this issue, we propose a novel unsupervised data augmentation technique that utilizes a generative adversarial network to synthesize realistic medical images. By leveraging this approach, we can generate a substantial amount of labeled data for training deep learning models. We evaluate the effectiveness of our method using the ACDC dataset for cardiac image segmentation, and our results demonstrate its superiority over existing state-of-the-art unsupervised data augmentation techniques.

We have developed a novel method to derive solutions for eleven-dimensional supergravity with a G2 structure, specifically in the presence of an NS5-brane. This approach builds upon the fundamental principles of BPS solutions and employs a 7-sphere ansatz, which we then utilize to solve the equation of Gauss-Bonnet surface. Notably, our findings yield a diverse set of solutions, including asymptotically flat, AdS7, and flat cases, as well as solutions with compactification on a spherical topology. These solutions exhibit a range of properties, including a finite action, a G2 structure, and a Ricci-flat metric.

Machine learning models are commonly affected by noisy labels, which can lead to poor performance and generalization. To mitigate this issue, researchers have developed various methods to identify and correct label errors. However, these approaches often struggle with large datasets due to their high computational cost. To address this challenge, a new approach called FastFix has been proposed, which efficiently identifies and corrects mislabeled instances within a small subset of the training data. FastFix achieves this by utilizing a combination of a random forest classifier and a gradient-based update mechanism to iteratively refine its estimates of label noise. Through extensive testing on multiple benchmark datasets, FastFix has been shown to significantly outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

The ground state wave function at filling factor $
u=1$ in the Quantum Hall effect is a key concept, yet its precise form remains unknown. This study explores the possibility of a localized, non-interacting electron in a 2D space, confined to a specific point, acting as the $
u=1$ state. By applying the Coulomb interaction to this setup, we derive an expression for the effective potential, which is then used to calculate the Hall conductivity. This approach yields a result consistent with the Thouless-Klauder formula, validating the assumption that the $
u=1$ state can be represented by a localized, non-interacting electron in a 2D space.

Recent advancements in language model pretraining have led to significant improvements in natural language understanding, but these gains have largely been driven by large-scale pretraining datasets and limited by the constraints of smaller models. To address this, we propose a new training strategy called METRO, which enables the effective training of large language models using a massive, multi-generational dataset. METRO's key innovation is a dynamic approach to model training, where each subsequent generation is fine-tuned to focus on underrepresented aspects of the language. We demonstrate the effectiveness of METRO by training a 1.3B parameter model, which outperforms its predecessors in a range of language understanding tasks.

We investigate the topological characteristics of a quantum network by examining its entropic properties, including von Neumann entropy and mutual information. Our research demonstrates that these measures can be used to determine the network's connectivity, with the specific case of a single qubit per node revealing the precise connections. Furthermore, we show that these measures can also reveal the network's modular structure, with the result that a quantum network's configuration can be fully deduced from a single measurement.

To effectively convey insights and findings through visual aids, it's crucial to provide clear explanations and context for each slide. This study explores how presenters can enhance the impact of their data visualizations by including accompanying text. We conducted a study where participants watched a presentation and then created their own visual aids based on the same information. Our findings show that including descriptive text in the visual aids is beneficial for understanding the content, and our analysis of the participants' work revealed several best practices for writing effective supporting text.

The behavior of a periodically driven many-body system is studied, where its ground state at high temperatures exhibits the properties of a classical gas. This is achieved by using a quantum model that can be mapped to a classical model through a process called "classicalization." Our research focuses on the classical behavior of this system, where we find that the steady state reached is the highest entropy state possible. This effect is observed in various systems, including those with finite and infinite dimensions, and is characterized by the presence of a "thermal fixed point." This phenomenon is also linked to the phenomenon of "many-body localization," and we find that the steady state reached is the same as the one obtained in localized systems.

We introduce counterfactual plans, a novel approach to crafting actions that mitigate biases in machine learning predictions by altering specific variables. Our method allows for the creation of plans that adapt to various classification methods and objectives, and can be applied to both discrete and continuous action spaces. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through a combination of theoretical and empirical evaluations, and showcase its practical application in identifying discriminatory loan decisions.

Urban sound classification is a crucial task for monitoring noise pollution, and deep learning models have shown impressive performance in this area. However, the development of deep learning models requires a large dataset of labeled sounds, which is often expensive and time-consuming to obtain. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach that uses a generative adversarial network to generate new training data from a small initial dataset. By leveraging this method, we can significantly reduce the need for human-annotated data and improve the accuracy of urban sound classification models. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, which can be used to fine-tune pre-trained models with a small amount of human-annotated data.

We investigate the properties of supersymmetric AdS4 black holes in a specific N=3 supergravity model, where we identify two types of AdS4 vacua with symmetries of SO(3) x SO(3) and SO(3). Our analysis shows that the supersymmetric configurations of these black holes are limited to specific points on the AdS4 vacua, and we identify the necessary conditions for these configurations to exist. These conditions are similar to those found in the case of four-dimensional supersymmetric black holes in M-theory and type IIA supergravity.

A new type of computing platform, Focal-plane Sensor-processors (FPSPs), is being developed to handle image signal processing and artificial intelligence tasks at the edge of networks. This innovative architecture is being explored for edge computation, offering several benefits, including low power consumption and real-time processing. However, it also presents challenges, such as limited resources and high variability in processing tasks. To address these issues, a novel approach called FocalUT is proposed, utilizing a combination of task partitioning and dynamic task scheduling. This method is based on a graph partitioning model and a dynamic programming algorithm, and it has been shown to significantly reduce energy consumption while meeting processing deadlines. Experimental results on a real-world image classification task demonstrate the effectiveness of FocalUT, achieving a 2.5 times improvement in energy efficiency compared to a baseline approach.

We investigate the connection between anomalies and global symmetries in effective field theories, specifically focusing on theories that include a $\theta$-term. Our research reveals that the presence of a $\theta$-term with a non-zero coefficient can lead to the presence of anomalous global symmetries, which are not detected by the effective action but rather by the measure of the theory. This phenomenon is not a result of the measure's sign ambiguity but rather a reflection of the theory's inherent properties. We provide several examples to illustrate this phenomenon and discuss its implications for theories that involve gauge symmetries, including the possibility of anomalous global symmetries in theories with spontaneously broken gauge symmetries.

In empirical game-theoretic analysis, researchers use real-world data to train an AI model that simulates game behavior. This model relies on an oracle, which provides feedback on the AI's performance by indicating whether its predictions are correct or not. However, finding an efficient oracle can be challenging due to the need for a large number of accurate labels. Our research focuses on developing a new approach to create an AI model that requires fewer labels to accurately predict game outcomes. We propose a method that leverages the idea of learning from the most uncertain predictions first, which we call Thompson Sampling with Label Filtering, or TS-LF. Our approach is based on the idea that the AI should prioritize learning from its most uncertain predictions, which are then filtered to ensure that only the most informative labels are obtained. Our experiments show that TS-LF outperforms traditional methods, such as Q-learning, in a variety of scenarios, and that it achieves this with significantly fewer labels required to achieve the same level of accuracy.

Aristotle's modal logic is examined, specifically his views on the modal syllogism. A novel modal logic is proposed, drawing from the paradigm of classical logic. This system is shown to be complete, normal, and compact, with respect to its axiomatisation. The logic is further explored in its relational aspects, where the concept of similarity is introduced as a fundamental notion. This leads to the establishment of a category of modal syllogisms that adhere to the principle of similarity. This system is shown to be a subset of the broader modal logic, and a method is proposed to embed the former within the latter.

Quantum correlations can be identified by violating classical causal inequalities, which are limits set on joint measurement outcomes. We've developed a method to detect causal quantum correlations using measurements on specific states, and found that certain devices can't reliably detect them, even with extremely high sensitivity. However, certain devices can be used to detect these correlations, and we've found that devices with high sensitivity of around 99.99% can be used to observe violations of up to 3.01.

In the HEVC/H.265 video coding standard, frame-level bit distribution is a crucial aspect. This paper proposes a novel bit allocation framework that integrates machine learning techniques to optimize video coding efficiency. The proposed method involves two stages: first, it employs a machine learning model to predict the optimal bit allocation for each frame based on its unique characteristics; second, it allocates bits to each coding structure node in a hierarchical manner, ensuring that the overall bit budget is met. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses the HEVC/H.265 bit allocation scheme, achieving a reduction of up to 14.4% with minimal impact on visual quality.

The C/O ratio in protoplanetary disks has been found to be significantly higher than in the Sun, with values ranging from 0.75 to 1.5. This elevated ratio is crucial in determining the chemical composition of these disks, particularly in relation to the abundance of C2H, a key species in understanding disk chemistry. In this study, we investigate the impact of the C/O ratio on the gas-phase chemistry of protoplanetary disks, using a one-dimensional disk model that accounts for the C/O ratio, in addition to the standard parameters. Our results show that the C/O ratio has a profound effect on the gas-phase chemistry of these disks, with a direct correlation between the ratio and the abundance of C2H, as well as other carbon-bearing species. This relationship is attributed to the increased production of C2H, CO, and CH4 in disks with higher C/O ratios, resulting in a decrease in gas-phase H2O and CH4. Our findings suggest that the C/O ratio is a critical factor in shaping the gas-phase chemistry of protoplanetary disks, and its measurement can provide valuable insights into the disk's physical and chemical properties.

Cutting planes play a vital role in solving complex mixed-integer linear problems (MILPs) as they allow for the refinement of the feasible region, enabling the identification of optimal solutions. The development of new cutting-plane families has significantly accelerated the resolution of MILPs. This paper introduces a novel cutting-plane method grounded in the concept of a convex hull of a fundamental set, which is applied to the convex hull of a fundamental set of 0/1 vectors. The proposed approach yields a cutting-plane set that is closed under affine transformations and provides a valid inequality for the convex hull of the set of 0/1 vectors. The efficacy of the new cutting-plane family is demonstrated through computational experiments conducted on a large-scale test set comprising 400 instances of the MAX-CUT problem.

Our research focuses on the investigation of the electronic properties of Ta$_{2-x}$Ir$_x$O$_5$N. Using a combination of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and theoretical calculations, we have identified a significant energy gap in the material, particularly at the M point, which is a key characteristic of topological semimetals. Furthermore, we have observed a unique band structure in the material, characterized by a distinct "butterfly" shape, which is a hallmark of the material's topological features. Our findings also suggest that the material undergoes a significant band inversion, resulting in the emergence of Dirac lines and Fermi arcs. These results provide strong evidence for the material's topological semimetallic nature.

Duplicate bug report detection in software development has become increasingly important due to the exponential growth of bug tracking systems. This growth has led to a significant number of duplicate bug reports, which can cause confusion and hinder the resolution of unique issues. Our research presents a new approach to detecting duplicate bug reports, which involves a hybrid method combining natural language processing and machine learning techniques. By incorporating both sentence and document-level features, our model achieves an accuracy rate of 94.4% in classifying bug reports from Mozilla's Bugzilla database.

We investigate the impact of anisotropy on the phase transition in a two-dimensional bond percolation model. The anisotropic network is created by adjusting the probability of connections in various directions. The study focuses on the phase transition caused by varying the probability of connections within the same direction and keeps other bond probabilities constant and equal to zero. The findings indicate that introducing anisotropy significantly reduces the critical connection probability and can even eliminate the phase transition if anisotropy is strong enough. The study also examines the cluster size distribution and percolation threshold under different anisotropy conditions.

A significant challenge in Named Entity Recognition (NER) is the scarcity of labeled data, particularly in resource-constrained settings. To address this issue, Distantly-Supervised NER (DS-NER) has been developed, leveraging pre-trained language models to generate pseudo labels for unseen data. However, these models often struggle with domain shift, resulting in inaccurate predictions. To mitigate this issue, we propose a new approach that utilizes a domain discriminator to identify the most domain-invariant representations. By doing so, we can isolate the representations that are most relevant to NER tasks, thereby improving the accuracy of DS-NER. Experimental results on multiple domain-shifted NER datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

The rapid expansion of social media has led to a significant increase in user-generated content, with Twitter being one of the most widely used platforms for social media sharing. The ability to analyze online user sentiment through social media data can provide valuable insights into how customers perceive a brand's products or services. This study aims to develop a sophisticated Twitter sentiment analysis model that incorporates a combination of deep learning and attention mechanisms. The proposed model, which utilizes a stacked transformer architecture, includes a feature extraction layer that utilizes a pre-trained BERT model, and a classification layer that utilizes a multi-head attention-based neural network. The model's effectiveness is evaluated using a publicly available Twitter dataset, and the results demonstrate the model's ability to achieve a high accuracy rate of 85.45% in classifying sentiment.

This research focuses on a class of materials with intricate structures, comprising a multitude of small, irregularly-shaped particles dispersed within a matrix. We investigate the thermal conductivity of these materials, accounting for both their internal heat transfer properties and the spatial arrangement of the particles. By employing a multiscale approach, we derive a simplified, macroscopic model that accurately captures the material's overall thermal behavior. The underlying assumptions and mathematical framework of this approach are thoroughly outlined.

The exoplanet CI Tau b, a Jupiter-like planet, orbits its host star at a relatively close distance. Notably, its orbital path is highly elliptical, suggesting that it formed farther from the star and migrated to its current position. This scenario is consistent with theoretical predictions, but further research is necessary to confirm the planet's origins. Observations of the planet's host star, made using the ALMA telescope, reveal that the star has a complex structure, with multiple rings and a dusty disk. This disk is likely the result of the planet's gravitational influence, and its composition is consistent with theoretical predictions. This study provides valuable insights into the planet's migration history and the impact it has on its host star's environment.

The circular orbit of a point particle in a central force field is examined, 
where the force exerted is directly proportional to the distance from the 
center of the system and inversely proportional to the first power of the 
distance. A novel analytical approach is employed to derive the equation of 
motion, which is distinct from the conventional Hamiltonian formalism. By 
utilizing this approach, the expression for force in relation to the particle's 
position is derived, revealing that it is proportional to the sine of the 
angle subtended at the center.

We establish a set of inequalities for fractional Sobolev spaces on compact Riemannian manifolds with bounded curvature. These inequalities surpass the standard fractional Ancona inequalities by incorporating additional terms that are linked to the manifold's curvature.

This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-object filtering, where trajectories of multiple objects are estimated over time. We present a new estimation method, based on particle trajectories, that outperforms existing techniques in terms of computational efficiency. Our approach involves two key innovations: a new particle selection method, utilizing a bipartite matching algorithm, and a more effective particle updater that leverages the entire trajectory of each particle. We demonstrate the superiority of our method in a simplified environment, where trajectories of multiple objects are repeated over time.

The growing presence of power electronics converters in AC networks has raised concerns about their impact on network stability. This is particularly true in scenarios where converters interact with existing infrastructure, potentially leading to resonance and instability issues. To address these concerns, this study focuses on the dynamic behavior of a converter connected to a network with a large number of poorly damped poles. By analyzing the system's behavior, we aim to identify the conditions under which the system remains stable and to understand the relationship between the number of unstable poles and the system's damping properties. Our research also explores the system's response to disturbances and the effectiveness of droop control methods in maintaining stability.

This paper examines the characteristics of online signature templates by introducing three new measures. These measures are based on the distances between the signature provider's handwritten and machine-generated signatures, as well as the distances between different real signatures produced by the same individual. The proposed measures are then evaluated in the context of online signature verification. Experimental results indicate that these measures can enhance the performance of online signature verification systems, particularly when combined with existing features.

The classic solution for calculating the number of lattice points in a triangle exists when all its vertices have integer coordinate values. This paper delves into the scenario where the triangle's vertices have coordinate values expressed as algebraic numbers. To address this, we employ a method that incorporates the use of integer lattice points in a modified polygon derived from the triangle, known as the modified triangle. This modified triangle is created by introducing new vertices that have coordinate values expressed as algebraic integers. This process is repeated until the resulting polygon consists of triangles with vertices having algebraic integer coordinate values. By counting the lattice points in this modified polygon, we can then determine the number of lattice points in the original triangle. This approach is exemplified through the use of triangles with coordinate values expressed as quadratic and cubic integers.

Mobile applications with numerous components and frequent updates require a context-aware approach to optimize performance and adapt to changing environments. Context-oriented programming (CoOP) is a suitable methodology for addressing this challenge, as it enables the separation of context-specific aspects and their flexible integration into mobile applications. However, CoOP's benefits are hindered by the need to manually manage the creation and handling of context variables, a task that is often overlooked in existing research. This paper addresses this limitation by introducing a new framework that simplifies the integration of context variables into mobile applications. The proposed framework leverages Android's reflection mechanism to simplify the creation and handling of context variables, and we demonstrate its effectiveness through a real-world example.

This paper introduces a novel pose estimation approach that integrates the attention mechanism. The proposed method, called the Attention-based Multi-head Mechanism (AMM), offers a unified framework for pose estimation tasks. AMM leverages the attention mechanism to dynamically weigh the importance of different feature channels. The approach also incorporates a multi-head mechanism to dynamically select relevant channels for each pose keypoint. The resulting method is straightforward to implement and yields superior performance on multiple datasets, surpassing state-of-the-art results.

A novel method for measuring the fluxes of astrophysical sources has been developed, leveraging the occultation of these sources by the Earth. This method involves tracking changes in observed counts when a source is visible versus hidden behind the Earth. The technique has been applied to a dataset of 12 sources, including black holes and pulsars, using data collected by the Fermi Large Area Telescope over a period of 10 years. The results demonstrate the potential of this approach for estimating source fluxes, with a notable example showing a significant increase in flux for one of the sources, aligning with previous observations. The method's sensitivity is constrained by the frequency of data collection and the duration of occultation. The technique has been applied to a dataset of 12 sources, including 7 black holes and 5 pulsars, yielding promising results.

The blockchain industry has been rapidly expanding, with numerous blockchain protocols and projects emerging, but their actual performance in real-world scenarios remains uncertain. Despite the growing interest, there is a significant knowledge gap in understanding how different protocols compare in terms of their practical usability. This study aims to bridge this gap by conducting a comprehensive analysis of 15 prominent blockchain protocols, evaluating their performance under various conditions. Our research involved a thorough examination of these protocols, considering factors such as their architecture, security guarantees, and implementation details. We then assessed their practical usability by analyzing their code, testing their security, and evaluating their performance in various scenarios. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of these protocols, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses, and offering insights into their potential applications.

Doubly heavy tetraquark states are considered prime candidates for the exotic states $T_{cc}$, $TT$, $TT'$, and $TT''$. In this study, we employed the QCD sum rule method to determine the mass of the $T_{cc}$ state with specific quantum numbers, and our results were in line with previous predictions. The analysis also revealed that the mass of the $T_{cc}$ state with $J^P=0^+$ is lower than that of the $T_{cc}^*$ state with $J^P=1^-$, and we calculated the mass of the $T_{cc}^*$ state with $J^P=1^-$. The results were compared to those obtained by other theoretical methods.

We investigate the metastability of the electroweak vacuum across a broad range of Higgs masses, encompassing both the Standard Model and Type II two Higgs doublet model. By analyzing the running Higgs mass, we identify a critical point at low energies where the Higgs mass transitions from metastable to stable. This boundary is determined by the Higgs mass's dependence on energy scale, with metastability prevailing at lower scales. We also examine the influence of new physics on this metastability phenomenon and find that it can significantly impact the Higgs mass's behavior, potentially shifting the critical point to lower energies.

This paper establishes a heat kernel lower bound for the ultrahyperbolic equation on the entire space and develops a heat flow on the positive side of the n-dimensional Lorentz-Minkowski space. Furthermore, we derive a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the associated heat flow and demonstrate the existence of global weak solutions to the ultrahyperbolic heat equation.

This paper examines the statistical properties of maximum likelihood-based estimators under a Bregman divergence framework, specifically under conditions of normality. We demonstrate that estimators belonging to the DPD class, which encompasses a range of estimators, are consistent under this framework. Additionally, our research shows that under certain conditions, such as those defined by Kullback-Leibler, Jeffreys, and Kullback-Leibler-Fan, the maximum likelihood-based estimators exhibit asymptotic normality under Bregman divergence.

We introduce a novel, self-supervised neural radiance model capable of generating novel views of dynamic, unstructured scenes. Our approach builds upon the neural radiance fields framework, incorporating a time-aware component to account for dynamic elements. To capture the complexity of dynamic scenes, we employ a sparse set of camera views and a high-resolution time representation. Our model is trained using a time-differentiated loss function that optimizes time and space simultaneously. To achieve this, we utilize a time-aware differentiable rendering function and a time-aware gradient operator. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of our model in synthesizing novel views of dynamic scenes, outperforming existing methods in terms of quality and generalizability.

We investigate the statistical behavior of chaotic quantum graphs with a specific focus on their most significant paths.  By analyzing the dynamics of classical particle motion, we identify the primary contribution to the quantum graphs' scattering matrix as coming from classical trajectories surrounding a small number of critical periodic paths.  By examining the scattering matrix of these periodic paths, we derive an expression that allows us to calculate the dominant terms in the scattering matrix of the entire graph, which we find to be proportional to the classical scattering matrix.  This result holds true for both the classical and quantum versions of the classical scattering matrix.  By applying this formula, we are able to show that the dominant terms in the scattering matrix of the graph are related to the classical scattering matrix.  This result has significant implications for the study of chaotic quantum graphs, where we find that the dominant terms in the scattering matrix are related to the classical scattering matrix.

Accurate determination of variable stars' periods is crucial for astronomers, particularly for understanding their characteristics and classifying them.  However, the large number of stars in modern astronomical surveys makes manual classification and period estimation impractical.  To address this issue, we have developed a new method that combines machine learning with the Period Finding by Artificial Neural Networks (PFANN) algorithm.  By training the algorithm on a dataset of 100,000 stars, we have achieved high accuracy in our results, with the algorithm able to correctly identify the periods of stars in the training set with a 99% success rate.  We have also tested our algorithm on a sample of stars from the OGLE-III survey and found that it performs well even when faced with noisy data.  Our method has the potential to greatly improve the accuracy of period estimates for variable stars in large astronomical surveys.

This paper explores the development of stable feedback control loops for complex systems with multiple degrees of freedom, using a method that prioritizes ease of implementation. It focuses on a specific class of systems known as negative imaginary systems, which can provide robust and high-performance control without the need for complex filters or computational steps. Our approach is based on a modified feedback design that ensures the closed-loop system meets the necessary conditions for stability, and we demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a simulation involving a 3D robotic arm.

The rapid advancement of deep learning has led to significant breakthroughs in computer vision, but it has also created a pressing need for a deeper understanding of the underlying processes. Recent studies have shown that neural networks can suffer from catastrophic interference, resulting in a decline in performance on previously learned tasks when new information is acquired. This paper investigates the potential of using knowledge distillation to mitigate catastrophic interference, focusing on the relationship between the number of training examples and the severity of interference. Our research reveals that the optimal number of training examples for a model to achieve stability depends on the number of tasks being learned, and we propose a novel approach to determine this optimal number. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in achieving stable learning and confirm that the model can be further fine-tuned to improve performance.

In multilingual settings, individuals frequently alternate between languages when communicating, often resulting in code-switching. This study focuses on code-switched text within the context of code-mixed social media, specifically examining the impact of language switching on the performance of text classification models. We explore the benefits and drawbacks of incorporating code-switched data into model training and how to effectively handle this type of input during inference. We also introduce a novel model that can handle code-switched text, built on the transformer architecture, and evaluate its performance on a dataset consisting of code-mixed English-Hindi tweets.

A new theory is proposed to address three major unsolved mysteries in particle physics and cosmology. The model involves a single scalar field with a specific potential that yields three distinct vacuum states, resulting in three corresponding phases that resemble the standard model, a left-handed model, and a right-handed model. The transition between these phases is marked by a significant, yet subtle, shift in the vacuum state, characterized by a specific scalar field value. The model's predictions are consistent with the observed universe and suggest the existence of a distinct, high-energy scale. The theory also predicts the existence of a specific scalar particle and a distinct signature in the Large Hadron Collider data. The model's predictions are further supported by a study of the muon's magnetic moment.

This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling user interactions with web applications, specifically focusing on the click-through rates of online advertisements. By leveraging deep learning techniques, our method outperforms its predecessors in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. To further enhance the model's interpretability, we incorporate a feature selection mechanism that identifies the most influential user attributes. To mitigate the model's susceptibility to data noise, we employ a regularized learning framework. Experimental validation on a substantial dataset of online advertisements from a prominent Chinese search engine demonstrates the proposed method's superiority over existing models in predicting click-through rates.

This research examines the performance benefits of using intelligent reflecting surfaces in cell-free networks for wireless communication. The study focuses on a specific scenario where the surface's phase shift accuracy is imperfect, and it does not have access to channel state information. The results show that even without perfect phase shift accuracy and channel state information, the use of intelligent reflecting surfaces can still provide a significant gain in network performance. The performance gain is found to be influenced by the number of base stations and the surface's phase shift accuracy. The study also finds that as the surface's phase shift accuracy improves, the potential network gain increases, and it becomes less dependent on the number of base stations.

Branch prediction plays a crucial role in modern computing systems, and recent advances in deep learning have led to the development of deep branch predictors (DBPs). This study introduces a new DBP that utilizes a neural network to predict branch outcomes and a dedicated hardware accelerator to support high-speed execution. The proposed accelerator is designed to minimize memory access overhead through the use of small, on-chip memory arrays that can be accessed in parallel. The results of our evaluation, which were conducted using a variety of benchmarks and a 16nm FPGA platform, demonstrate the effectiveness of the DBP approach and show that it outperforms traditional branch predictors across a range of performance metrics.

Active visual monitoring is a crucial component in various applications such as surveillance, traffic monitoring, and self-driving vehicles. This research focuses on developing an efficient method for active monitoring, which involves identifying the most informative objects to track in real-time. A novel approach is proposed that combines a deep network for object detection and tracking, and a decision-making strategy to determine which objects warrant the most attention. The proposed method is trained using a combination of imitation learning and a customized reward function, which simulates real-world tracking scenarios. The approach is tested on multiple datasets and compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying relevant objects and reducing tracking errors.

In the SOS model on Cayley tree, we've recently discovered new solutions to the boundary law, which are distinct from the semi-invariant solutions previously found. These new solutions can be expressed as a combination of a Markov chain and an additional invariant component. We've developed a method to analyze the new boundary law by utilizing the generating functions of Markov chains. This approach has been successfully applied to a broad range of SOS models, including those with additive interactions. Additionally, we've established a key criterion for determining when the Markov chain is in fact a degenerate random walk.

In a study, we investigate the influence of temporal entanglement on the energy transfer between two nonlinear optical systems. Our analysis shows that the generation of virtual photons through temporal entanglement can lead to enhanced frequency correlations, resulting in increased energy transfer efficiency. Furthermore, we find that the optimal energy transfer occurs when the frequency correlation is maximized. Notably, this phenomenon is independent of the distance between the two nonlinear optical systems.

We have calculated the strong coupling constants for various mesons with light and heavy quarks, including the charmed and bottom mesons, using the light-cone instant form of relativistic quark models. Our approach involves a relativistic model that accounts for the mesons' wave functions in the transverse space, yielding results consistent with previous studies and other theoretical models. The calculated coupling constants for certain mesons, such as the rho and K mesons, match the values obtained from QCD sum rules and full QCD lattice simulations.

The DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments are poised to make groundbreaking contributions to neutrino physics, solving outstanding mysteries in the field. By doing so, they will not only resolve the remaining neutrino physics questions, but also provide valuable insights into the properties of matter and the universe. The two experiments will employ different approaches to achieve their goals, but they share a common objective of advancing our knowledge in the neutrino sector. The following discussion will highlight the unique aspects of each project, emphasizing their potential to explore the neutrino mass hierarchy and the universe's fundamental nature.

In non-experimental studies, researchers often employ statistical methods to
compensate for imbalances in data by using linear regression models. These
methods typically rely on a set of influential covariates to minimize disparities
between treatment and control groups. However, the effectiveness of such
adjustments is often constrained by the limitations of available data. This
paper explores the potential for utilizing machine learning techniques to
improve covariate balance, with a focus on the application of neural networks
and support vector machines. Our results indicate that these methods can be
successful in achieving covariate balance and that their performance is
competitive with traditional approaches.

This study presents a model-free approach to damping control for power systems, 
utilizing a control strategy based on a data-driven method. The proposed control 
system uses a data-driven model to identify and mitigate local and inter-area 
oscillations. The effectiveness of this control is demonstrated through simulations 
on the IEEE 68-bus system, highlighting its ability to work with uncertain system 
models.

We investigate the simultaneous decay of multiple atoms, examining its influence on the collective light emitted by the ensemble. This phenomenon is significant in the context of quantum emitters, such as atoms, molecules, and defects, as well as nanophotonic cavities. We derive a comprehensive expression for the collective light emitted by a large group of identical quantum emitters, considering the effects of spontaneous emission, interference, and the simultaneous decay of multiple emitters. Our findings are applicable to a wide range of systems, including atomic ensembles, nanophotonic cavities, and quantum dots. We also explore the potential for harnessing the enhanced light emitted by large ensembles to create compact, high-performance light sources for various applications.

We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion for the local asymptotic stability of kinks when subjected to odd disturbances. This criterion is met if and only if the KdV equation's linearized operator at the kink level has a non-tangential degenerate kernel. This criterion is consistent with the one we previously proposed for the KdV equation's linearized operator around a kink in the context of small odd perturbations. Our criterion is also applicable to the Degasperis-Procesi equation, a higher-order modification of the KdV equation.
This document provides an overview of our research on color transparency within the Proton Electric Dipole Form Factor experiment at JLab.

This paper introduces a consistency training approach tailored for multi-modal
learning. The proposed method employs two data augmentation techniques: one for the
visual inputs and another for the text features. The visual inputs are manipulated
using a combination of random resizing, cropping, and normalization, while text
features are augmented by randomly inserting or deleting words. The visual and
text inputs are then fed into separate encoders, with a shared fully connected
layer. The shared layer is trained to produce consistent outputs for both
augmented inputs. The model's ability to generate consistent visual and text
representations is further enhanced by a contrastive loss function, which is
calculated using the augmented inputs. The proposed method is evaluated on the
Charades dataset and achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a significant
improvement of 2.5% over existing methods.

The precise localization of polyps in gastrointestinal endoscopy videos is a critical task in computer-assisted endoscopy. Current methods, however, rely on a single video frame, which are insufficient in capturing the polyp's shape and size due to variations across frames and artifacts. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach called Polyp CenterNet, which utilizes a center-based network to predict the center of polyps in a single frame, and then aggregates information from multiple frames to enhance the accuracy. Our method incorporates a novel attention module to mitigate inter-frame variations and a center loss function to reduce the impact of artifacts. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, which outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy.

A novel unequal probability sampling approach has been developed, which enables the selection of a diverse set of samples based on a range of specified criteria. The method involves two key components: a variable window that adjusts its size based on the selected samples, and a mechanism to evaluate the diversity of potential samples within that window. The algorithm then selects a diverse set of representative samples by iteratively expanding the window and choosing a diverse subset of samples until the desired level of diversity is achieved. Theoretical analysis and simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in achieving diverse samples.

The half-life of $^{57}$Zn has been measured using the Recoil Separation After Capture of Thermal-energized Atoms (RESCONTA) facility at the University of Texas at Austin. A 1.8 MeV $^{57}$Zn activity was determined by analyzing the $\beta^+$ branching ratio in the $\beta^+$ decay of $^{57}$Cu, which was obtained by stopping $^{57}$Cu ions at a degrader. The result, which is an average of multiple measurements, shows that $^{57}$Zn has a half-life of 8.9 seconds with a margin of error of 0.2 seconds. This measurement is consistent with prior research but also provides a more precise calculation.

We establish an infinite hierarchy of logarithmic Abel-Jacobi maps originating from cycles of higher codimensions within abelian schemes over integer rings, which can be expressed in terms of higher codimension cycle classes. This series is shown to be compatible with reduction maps, and we derive a universal abelian scheme that captures the universal properties related to these higher Abel-Jacobi maps. This scheme serves as an extension of Tate's abelian scheme that computes the Abel-Jacobi maps associated with 0-cycles.

Pulsars are highly magnetized and rapidly rotating neutron stars that emit electromagnetic radiation through their interaction with their surroundings. Pulsar wind nebulae, formed by the interaction of pulsar winds with surrounding material, are significant sources of electromagnetic radiation across various parts of the spectrum. The study of these nebulae has led to the discovery of several key properties of pulsars, including their spin-down luminosity and surface magnetic field strength. The investigation of these nebulae has also provided insights into the complex physics governing their behavior. The aim of this review is to summarize the current understanding of pulsar wind nebulae, highlighting recent findings and future research directions.

This study examines the long-term behavior of solutions to certain types of partial differential equations, specifically those involving chemical reactions and diffusion in complex systems. We investigate systems governed by equations of the following form: a specific equation for a single variable and a general equation for multiple variables in a confined space. We focus on systems where the reaction terms are limited and the initial conditions are stable, and prove the existence of key patterns in these systems. We also show that these patterns are stable over time and that they represent the ultimate states of these solutions.

The Hubble Space Telescope's Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3) is a powerful tool for capturing high-resolution images of the universe. Its ability to capture both near-infrared and visible light images makes it an ideal instrument for studying the properties of Ultra-compact dwarfs (UCDs) and Globular Clusters (GCs). These celestial bodies are of great interest due to their unique characteristics and proximity to the center of galaxies. In this study, we utilized WFC3's capabilities to analyze the structural and dynamical properties of UCDs and GCs within the Andromeda galaxy (M31). Our research involved comparing the structural parameters of these objects to their corresponding velocity dispersions, and we discovered that UCDs and GCs exhibit distinct relationships between these variables. Furthermore, we found that UCDs tend to have lower velocity dispersions than GCs, even at similar radii, which may indicate a difference in their formation mechanisms.

Recommender Systems have become ubiquitous in our daily lives, influencing our purchasing decisions and consumption habits. Despite their widespread adoption, developing a robust Recommender System is a complex task due to the inherent challenges of data sparsity, bias, and cold-start problems. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of Recommender Systems, highlighting their evolution, key techniques, and the pressing issues that still require attention. We delve into the underlying difficulties of Recommender Systems, the research trends that have emerged in recent years, and the promising directions for future research. Our analysis also touches on the applications of Recommender Systems in real-world scenarios, their integration with emerging technologies like blockchain and NLP, and the potential risks associated with their increasing reliance.

This study examines the asymptotic behavior of the standardized truncated test statistic under high dimensions, when the underlying distribution has a finite mean and covariance matrix, and is symmetric. We derive the limiting distribution for the standardized truncated test statistic under specific conditions on the threshold value c, relative to the distribution's tail index. For the case of standard normal distribution, we provide a precise threshold c, while for the case of general heavy-tailed distributions, we propose a threshold c, and provide conditions for the limiting distribution.

A novel Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system has been successfully developed to control complex robotic movements using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. The BCI system was tested in a real-world environment by having a subject operate a robotic wheelchair. The findings indicate that the BCI system can translate brain activity into specific movements, such as forward and reverse motions, using a proportional control model. The BCI system's performance was evaluated using various measures, including speed, accuracy, and stability, and the results show that the user can control the robotic wheelchair with high precision and speed. The BCI system's performance was also compared to a standard proportional control model and the results show that the BCI system outperforms it in terms of speed and accuracy. The BCI system's capabilities were also demonstrated in a real-world scenario where the user navigated the robotic wheelchair around obstacles. The BCI system's performance was evaluated using a measure of success and the results show that the user achieved a high success rate of 85% in navigating the robotic wheelchair around obstacles.

We've developed a novel approach to calculate the two-point function in the simplest conformal field theories, which involve a single primary field, through the use of a distributional inversion formula. This straightforward method is analogous to the lightcone perturbation theory and can be easily adapted to compute the twist-4 correlation functions in the conformal bootstrap problem.

A kidney transplant is a vital procedure for patients with end-stage renal disease, allowing them to live normally again. However, the process is complicated when a donor's kidney is incompatible with the recipient's immune system. To overcome this issue, researchers have been exploring the use of incompatible kidney transplants, which have been made possible through desensitization techniques. To determine the effectiveness of these transplants, researchers have been analyzing patient survival rates. This study aims to investigate the survival rates of patients who received kidney transplants from incompatible donors using a new machine learning approach. This approach involves analyzing survival rates for patients who received transplants from both compatible and incompatible donors, using a new machine learning model that can predict patient survival rates. The study found that the proposed model outperformed existing models in predicting patient survival rates.

This study compares the performance of two sequence modeling techniques, Hidden Markov Models and Long Short-Term Memory Models, in predicting the behavior of complex systems. By analyzing the behavior of the US labor market, the researchers investigated the accuracy of these models in predicting unemployment rates and the length of time it takes for the economy to recover from recessions. They found that while both models were effective, the Hidden Markov Model was more accurate in short-term predictions and the Long Short-Term Memory Model was more accurate in longer-term predictions.

This research focuses on the boundedness of a specific type of generalized Volterra integral operators, which act on weighted Lebesgue spaces, particularly in cases where the kernel has a singular integral over a finite interval. We establish the conditions under which these operators are bounded from one weighted space to another and provide a detailed characterization of their behavior.

In the field of experience management, a significant challenge arises from the need to analyze vast amounts of data from various sources, often with limited labels. To address this, we've developed a novel approach that combines data from multiple sources and tasks to improve model performance. By leveraging data from multiple sources, we've created a unified representation that enhances model accuracy and reduces the requirement for labels. The proposed method has been successfully applied to two real-world datasets and has demonstrated substantial improvements in model performance, with accuracy increases of up to 10% and label-reduction rates of up to 3 times.

High energy physics researchers rely heavily on data-driven approaches, making data an essential component of their research. In recent years, there has been a significant shift towards open data policies, driven by the recognition of its value in advancing science, breaking down disciplinary barriers, and benefiting society as a whole. This chapter in the Snowmass 2021 white papers series delves into the open data revolution and explores its implications for the high energy physics community. It examines current initiatives, addresses associated concerns, and makes recommendations to foster a culture of openness with data.

This paper introduces decomposed Richelot isogenies and examines their properties. These decomposed Richelot isogenies enable the creation of a modified Richelot isogeny graph, which retains essential characteristics of the original Richelot isogeny graph. As a result, it offers a more efficient approach to traversing the original graph and generating isogenies between curves with composite degree.

Recent studies have suggested that hot subdwarfs may possess magnetic fields, but the extent of this phenomenon remains unclear. To investigate, we conducted a thorough analysis of 12 magnetic hot subdwarfs using the ESPaDOnS and HARPS polarimeters. Our research yielded the first polarimetric measurements for 10 of these stars, while we refined existing data for the remaining two. The results indicate that the majority of these stars exhibit a significant magnetic field, with estimated surface strengths ranging from 1.5 to 7.5 kilogauss. By examining the distribution of magnetic field strengths, we found that the lower limit of the magnetic field distribution is approximately 1.5 kilogauss, suggesting that at least 50% of hot subdwarfs may possess a magnetic field.

In statistics and machine learning, particularly in the field of Gaussian process regression, positive semi-definite matrices play a crucial role. This paper focuses on a new approach to constructing a set of positive semi-definite functions based on a given positive semi-definite matrix. The method involves a specific type of matrix multiplication and retains the original matrix's rank. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly enhance the scalability of Gaussian process regression models.

Wikipedia's content is initially drafted in wikitext, but the online platform displays articles using HTML, which is based on the MediaWiki markup language. As an extension of the study in question, this research explores the differences between the two formats and assesses the accuracy of automated wikitext-to-HTML and vice versa translation. The analysis reveals that HTML better captures the online version's content and that accurate conversions between the two formats are achievable with a high degree of precision.

Recent advancements in the study of twisted bilayers have revealed the potential for novel electronic states and unique properties. A notable example is the observation of a moiré superlattice in hBN bilayers, which exhibits distinct characteristics. In contrast, bilayers of other materials, such as hexagonal boron nitride and transition metal dichalcogenides, have been found to exhibit polarization properties. A theoretical framework has been developed to explain the polarization in these bilayers, which arises from the breaking of symmetry due to the formation of a moiré superlattice. A proposed experiment involves measuring the polarization in these bilayers, which can be done using a technique that involves detecting changes in the polarization's phase. The results of the experiment can be used to determine the parameters of the moiré potential and the Berry phase of the material.

The nature of the universe's spatial curvature is a key unresolved issue in modern cosmology, and we propose a novel approach to address this question by combining data from the CMB, galaxy surveys, and gravitational wave observations. Our research demonstrates that the cosmological model, particularly in its ability to utilize the late-time universe's spatial curvature, is surprisingly resilient to the presence of unknown new physics that could potentially arise at the cosmic horizon. We further show that the combination of CMB, galaxy surveys, and gravitational wave observations can effectively constrain the universe's curvature, and we present a preliminary forecast for future observations. Our findings suggest that the upcoming generation of surveys will provide significant insights into the nature of the universe's spatial curvature, and we believe that the results will be crucial in shedding light on the mysteries surrounding the cosmos.

We investigate the movement of colloidal particles within nematic liquid crystals confined to tiny channels, and derive an equation that describes their behavior over time. This equation is based on the idea that the particles' motion is influenced by specific energy patterns, and we use this understanding to analyze the particles' behavior in different scenarios. Furthermore, we develop a new method to calculate the energy patterns, known as the Landau-de Gennes potential, from the particles' movement patterns.

The surface topography of asteroids can be significantly altered by close encounters with planets. To study this effect, researchers simulated the surface topography of an elongated asteroid after a close encounter with Earth using the Mohawk model. The results show that the surface slope and stress of the asteroid exhibit substantial variations, especially in the equatorial region, due to the uneven gravitational pull of the planet. The maximum stress and surface slope changes are more pronounced in longer and thinner asteroids. The duration of the encounter and the asteroid's distance from the planet also impact the magnitude of these changes, with the maximum stress and surface slope variations occurring at a certain distance and time.

Biomolecular systems frequently undergo spontaneous structural rearrangements that play a crucial role in their functioning. These spontaneous rearrangements can be triggered by various factors, such as changes in temperature or the presence of specific molecules. A new theoretical framework has been developed to study these spontaneous rearrangements, which involves a two-step process. First, the system is in a state of dynamic equilibrium, and then it transitions into a distinct configuration. This framework can be applied to a range of complex systems, such as those governed by Markov state models or those characterized by non-equilibrium dynamics. A key aspect of this framework is its ability to identify the underlying patterns of these spontaneous rearrangements, which can be visualized as networks of interconnected transitions. This framework has been successfully applied to study the structural rearrangements that occur in the HIV capsid, revealing new insights into its behavior.

The ice thickness distribution, represented by $g(h)$, is crucial for understanding the evolution of sea ice, but it is often overlooked in favor of the ice age distribution, $N(a)$. In this study, we derive an analytical solution for $g(h)$ from the linearized master equation, and find that it differs significantly from the traditional Pareto distribution. Our results show that as the ice thins, $g(h)$ shifts towards a single value, reflecting the ice's uniform thickness, and that the ice's thickness variability is directly linked to its overall age.

In this study, we identify and analyze the generalized Weierstrass semigroup 
associated with points on algebraic curves in complex projective space, 
specifically those defined over complex projective space. Our findings 
generalize and expand upon previous research by T. Kaji and A. Sharma in the 
context of non-complex, one-dimensional algebraic varieties.

Recent breakthroughs in singing voice synthesis have led to more authentic results, driven by advancements in deep learning and speech technology. This paper introduces a novel singing voice synthesis method that leverages a singing speech dataset to train a generative model, allowing for the creation of entirely new songs with customizable vocalists and lyrics. This approach eliminates the need for a middle-stage melodic model, simplifying the synthesis process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique by applying it to a real-world scenario, where we generate a new song using a pre-existing melody and lyrics. Furthermore, we examine the impact of varying acoustic and coarticulatory characteristics on the synthesized singing voices.

The development of birdsong detection and classification techniques has been hindered by the scarcity of comprehensive datasets featuring both annotated recordings and corresponding metadata. To address this issue, we have compiled the Birdsong21 dataset, comprising 1,500 hours of recordings annotated at the segment level. These segments are further categorized into 1,100 hours of bird calls and 400 hours of non-bird sounds. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our baseline models in identifying bird calls and separating them from non-bird sounds. Additionally, we have made our dataset and code available to foster advancements in this field.

We introduce a novel neural network-based approach to event camera calibration, 
utilizing image reconstruction as a more efficient alternative to traditional 
calibration techniques that rely on pattern projection. Our method involves 
capturing a 3D scene with a moving object and utilizing a neural network to 
generate a 2D image from the event data, thereby eliminating the need for 
external calibration tools. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this 
approach, which we also extend to 3D reconstruction by applying the concept 
of image matching. Our implementation is open-source and available for public 
use at the link: https://github.com/keerthivasan/ecco

Graph learning involves analyzing data represented as nodes and edges. Unlike traditional tabular data, graph learning requires a deeper understanding of the underlying data structures, which is often overlooked in the standard practice of using pre-built models. This paper proposes a new approach called G-Analyzer, designed to help users grasp graph-structured data. G-Analyzer employs a novel method to generate visualizations of sub-graphs, highlighting the most critical nodes and edges. By analyzing these sub-graphs, users can identify patterns and relationships that may be hidden in the original data, and even develop new features. We demonstrate the effectiveness of G-Analyzer through a series of experiments on real-world datasets, and show that it enhances the performance of graph neural networks.

We provide a comprehensive classification of unique weak del Pezzo surfaces that possess an exceptional divisor with a singular point, based on the surface's automorphism group. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for any weak del Pezzo surface, it is feasible to construct a generalised version of the surface by replacing the exceptional divisor with a singular curve.

A novel image-guided robot-assisted surgery system is proposed for retinal procedures. This system leverages a deep learning-based approach to image processing, enabling the creation of a 3D surface model from fundus images for intraocular tumor removal.
